jobs.title: Career Development Research Fellowship
jobs.description: Career Development Research Fellowships for full-time research offered by St John’s College to early career researchers who have recently completed or are close to completion of a doctorate (and will have submitted their thesis no later than three months before their start date of this post), or who have recently been awarded a doctorate. They provide an unrivalled opportunity to establish a research profile as a member of a collegiate community.St John’s College Oxford proposes, to elect up to Six such Fellows, with effect from 1st October 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter, one in each of the following subjects:Economics–Economists in any field are welcome to apply, but we particularly welcome applicants working on the economics of science, research policy, or higher education. We interpret these areas broadly and welcome theoretical and empirical work, including experimental and quasi-experimental research and the design and evaluation of policy interventions. As part of this element of the role, the postholder may be offered the opportunity to work with the Fellow for Research on coordinating events and seminars relevant to their fieldAsian and Middle Eastern Studies -this post will have a focus on Modern Arabic Literature with a life writing element.Anthropology of Forced Migration–Applicants for this post will be expected to have an active research record in the field of forced migration, demonstrated by publications commensurate with their stage of career.Philosophy–Open Area of Specialisation. Applicants for Philosophy will be required to submit written work with their initial application as well as an up-to-date CV.Human SciencesBiomedical Sciences –For Further information about this post please seeherePlease see thefurther particularsand details of how to apply below, except for the subjects separately linked in the list above.Candidates must indicate for which subject they are applying. Interdisciplinary applications will be allocated within this list of subjects at the discretion of the College.Career Development Research Fellowships are fixed-term posts, tenable for four years from the 1st October 2027, the start date of a Fellowship may, with the agreement of the college, be brought forward or delayed in exceptional cases, to accommodate personal circumstances; if so, the terminal date will be adjusted accordingly.The annual salary is equivalent to point 7.5 on the University Scale (currently £42,254) plus a pensionable £1,730 per annum Oxford University Weighting payment which will be paid in equal monthly instalments and pro-rated for part time appointments. The appointee will automatically be enrolled in the Universities Superannuation Scheme pension. Further details can be found here -USSApplications should be submitted electronically via this website, where detailed instructions on how to complete the application can be found:https://st-johns.resfell.co.uk/rf_2027/Please refer to theFurther particulars.

jobs.description: Department of PhilosophyTenure-Track Assistant Professor in Political PhilosophyThe Department of Philosophy at the College of the Holy Cross invites applications for a full-time tenure-track Assistant Professor specializing in Political Philosophy to begin in August 2027. The ideal candidate will have an Area of Specialization in Political Philosophy with an emphasis on the foundations of democracy. Within this AOS, we plan to look for Areas of Concentration in deliberative democracy, epistemological aspects of democracy, philosophy of law, pluralism, and non-state democracy. We expect such a candidate to meet needs at both the departmental and institutional level by teaching courses in the above-mentioned areas and perhaps by participating in interdisciplinary courses and related activities and programs offered by the College. Successful candidates will demonstrate excellence as both teachers and scholars. As teachers, we seek candidates with a demonstrated commitment toinnovative, inclusive excellence in teaching.  As scholars, we seek candidates with an active, fruitful research agenda who are cognizant of our obligations to the wider community.This position carries a 3-2 teaching load with a research leave prior to tenure review of either a full year at 80% salary or a semester at full salary, and generous sabbatical and fellowship leaves for tenured faculty. To enable a smooth transition to Holy Cross, new full-time tenure-track Assistant Professors receive start-up funding to support their research and professional development and have a one-course reduction in their first year of teaching (i.e., 2-2). This position offers full benefits and a starting salary of $102,500.In alignment with the strategic plans forHoly Crossandthe division of Academic Affairs, we view academic excellence and inclusive excellence as inextricably linked. Our faculty combine high-impact scholarship and outstanding teaching with a deep commitment to inclusive excellence. They generate new knowledge in their fields while utilizing evidence-based teaching strategies and course designs to create classroom environments where all students have a sense of belonging, are valued, and can flourish to reach their full potential. Academic freedom is a cornerstone of our intellectual and moral community; the College is committed to supporting faculty and students as they work to advance our educational mission and serve the common good.QUALIFICATIONSCandidates must demonstrate excellence in scholarship and undergraduate teaching as well as a commitment to inclusive pedagogies. A Ph.D. in Philosophy is required by the beginning of the appointment.APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONSPlease submit1. A cover letter addressing the position requirements listed above as well as the ways you might contribute to and further theCollege’s missionas a Jesuit, undergraduate liberal arts college and its core commitmentto creating a communitywhere every individual feels empowered to contribute their talents and perspectives. 2. A curriculum vitae.  3. Unofficial undergraduate and graduate transcripts. 4. A statement of your teaching philosophy and interests, with particular emphasis on how you utilize evidence-based teaching strategies to foster inclusive, high-belonging classroom environments. 5. 3 Confidential Letters of Recommendation 6. A Writing Sample (preferably published, but can be ‘in process’ as well) 7. A Research statement that communicates the candidate's current scholarly focus and future trajectoryThe College of the Holy Cross uses Interfolio to collect all faculty job applications. Please submit all materials tohttps://apply.interfolio.com/193949.For full consideration, please apply by November 1. Initial interviews via Zoom will take place in December 5-8, and campus visits for finalists will take place in February 9-18. Questions about this search may be directed to Professor Jeffrey Bernstein,[email protected].The Provost’s Office supportsthe Association of American Universities’ principleson preventing sexual harassment in academia. Accordingly, all finalists will be asked to attest that they are not currently under investigation for sexual misconduct and that there are no substantiated findings of sexual misconduct against them in any previous position—or, if such findings exist, to provide a full explanation. The candidate selected for an offer will also be asked to provide written consent for the release of personnel information from their prior employer.For applicants who may require visa sponsorship: The College supports new faculty in pursuing an appropriate visa or other immigration status consistent with their qualifications and the responsibilities of the position. Because several pathways may be available, the College works with candidates who are offered positions to determine the most appropriate option. Please note, however, the College does not support H-1B visa petitions that are subject to the payment of an additional $100,000 fee. The College, where appropriate, will support H-1B petitions that are not subject to the $100,000 fee.COLLEGE OF THE HOLY CROSSThe College of the Holy Cross is a highly selective Catholic liberal arts college in the Jesuit tradition. It enrolls about 3,200 students and is located in Worcester, Massachusetts—New England’s second-largest city.The College seeks faculty members who demonstrate an enduring commitment to academic excellence and inclusive excellence and who embrace the educational benefits of a richly diverse community. To learn more about faculty life at the College and in the Worcester area, applicants are encouraged to visit ourOffice of the Provost pageand ourFaculty Openings page.EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYMENT STATEMENTThe College is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer and complies with all Federal and Massachusetts laws concerning equal opportunity in the workplace.

jobs.description: Full Time Faculty, Assistant Professor in Philosophy, School of Social Sciences (SOSS)The School of Social Sciences, Singapore Management University, invites applications for two positions at the Assistant Professor rank (education track). Candidates must have expertise and research interests in either moral philosophy, political philosophy, social philosophy, or comparative philosophy. Candidates must also be able to teach an introductory course in critical thinking. The ability to teach introductory ethics is also highly desirable.These positions require a doctorate in Philosophy and teaching experience at the tertiary level. jobs.description: The Environmental Policy and Culture Program (EPC) at Northwestern University invites applications for two (2) full-time, three-year visiting assistant professorships, to begin September 1, 2027. EPC is an interdisciplinary undergraduate program with over 100 majors and minors, focusing on social scientific and humanistic approaches to environmental subjects.These positions are open in terms of period and geographic focus, but we are especially interested in interdisciplinary approaches to environmental decision-making and storytelling; policy and governance at local, national, and international scales; environmental economics; and environmental philosophy. We are also interested in professional or applied knowledge and experience in the fields of legal studies, philosophy, economics, and geography. The VAPs will each teach five courses a year, at least three of which should be distinct classes (some classes could be taught twice in the same year). The VAPs will also be encouraged to take part in the life of the program, including attending program events, mentoring students, and other forms of community building.The positions come with access to significant course development funding and we encourage candidates to think creatively about guest speakers, classroom technology, student experiences outside of the classroom, and other course enhancements.Candidates should have received a PhD in a humanities or social science field or have equivalent professional experience by the position start date, and have significant experience teaching at the college level.To apply please provide a cover letter, CV, research statement, teaching statement, evidence of teaching experience, and the names and email addresses of two references using Northwestern'sFaculty Recruiting Portal. In order to receive full consideration, applications must be received by October 30, 2026. Questions can be directed toKeith Woodhouse.Northwestern University is an equal opportunity, affirmative action employer and does not discriminate against qualified individuals on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, parental status, marital status, age, disability, citizenship status, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected class. We actively seek to encourage individuals from all diverse backgrounds to apply. For more information, please see the University’s Policy on Institutional Equity. jobs.description: Classification/Academic Level: Academic Level B (Lecturer)Salary package: $124,638 - $ 141,317 per annum plus 17% superannuation.Terms: 2 X Full-time, ContinuingCommencement: Flexible with a preference for the first half of 2027.Areas of Specialisation:Position 1: Ethics and/or social and political philosophy.Position 2: Open with Philosophy and AI as an area of competence.The Position:The School is looking to appoint two outstanding scholars whose expertise will complement the School’s existing strengths. Both appointees will be expected to carry out world-leading research resulting in regular publications in leading venues, contribute to the School’s stellar teaching program, supervise HDR students, apply for external grants, and be available for service roles as appropriate. At least one of the appointees will work in ethics and/or social and political philosophy. The other will work in any area that complements the School’s existing strengths, including the capacity to contribute to teaching in Philosophy and AI.The SchoolThe School of Philosophy, Research School of Social Sciences, is a world-leading department that combines several of the world's most cited living philosophers with dynamic and award-winning mid-career and early career researchers. ANU philosophers enjoy what is widely recognized as one of the world’s best environments for research and teaching in Philosophy. Our principal strengths are in moral and political philosophy, philosophy of science (especially philosophy of biology, probability, and decision theory), and philosophy of mind and psychology. We have a proud reputation of repeatedly winning significant support for both individual- and team-projects from the Australian Research Council, and every year welcome many international visitors to Canberra, hosting multiple workshops each year, as well as a vibrant series of weekly research seminars and reading groups. We have a constant flow of postdoctoral researchers, who go on to continuing positions at leading departments worldwide. We have three major research Centres— the Centre for Moral, Social and Political Theory, the Centre for Philosophy of the Sciences, and the Centre for Consciousness.The CollegeThe ANU College of Arts and Social Sciences (CASS) is the largest of the six Colleges at ANU. It is structured into two main research schools, offers degrees in more than 20 discipline areas and excels in research across the humanities and social sciences. The College has a substantial international research presence and is a major source of national policy advice. Our academic staff are internationally recognised for their research, and many are members of the Australian Academy of the Humanities, the Academy of the Social Sciences of Australia, or both. A hub of vibrant activity, we host numerous lectures, concerts and exhibitions each year, most of which are open to the public. Our students, staff and graduates come from more than 60 nations, bringing a diversity of perspective to campus life.Canberra is one of the world's finest places to live, with a rare combination of urban comfort and access to some of the most beautiful countryside in the world (including an easy drive to some of the world's best, and quietest, beaches). jobs.description: Position Title: Endowed Bartlett Chair Professor/Associate Professor, Free SpeechReq ID: R0006507Time Type: Full timeLocation: Waltham, MADescription:Job Description SummaryBentley University invites applications for the Bartlett Chair of Free Speech, an endowed position at the Associate or Full Professor level, to begin in Fall 2027.Funded by a generous gift from Bruce and Patricia Bartlett, this professorship affirms Bentley's commitment to fostering free expression, intellectual pluralism, and the constructive exchange of ideas as central to a liberal education.This position is part of a broader Bartlett Initiative that also includes a companion Chair of Free Enterprise. The two chairs will work together to develop programming, events, and curricular initiatives under the Bartlett banner that promote inquiry, debate, and engagement across disciplines.The Bartlett Chair of Free Speech carries a 1-1 teaching load and receives substantial support for scholarship, professional engagement, and leadership of the Bartlett Initiative. This support includes summer salary, a chair stipend, and a generous research and travel account.QualificationsCandidates are expected to demonstrate a strong and sustained commitment to the value and principles of free speech in their academic work.A successful candidate will demonstrate:A PhD in History, Philosophy, Political Science, Law, or a closely related field.A distinguished record of research, teaching, and public engagement appropriate to appointment at the Associate or Full Professor level.An active, high-quality research agenda with a direct and substantive connection to free speech, free expression, or closely related areas.Strength in interdisciplinary teaching and dialogue across fields.Evidence of active and visible engagement in their discipline and in broader scholarly, professional, civic, or public conversations related to free speech.We especially welcome candidates whose work engages:Cultural history, intellectual history, or political thought.First Amendment law or theories of expression.Academic freedom, civil discourse, or democratic institutions.Candidates with experience in public-facing scholarship, civic dialogue, media engagement, or leading campus and community conversations are particularly encouraged to apply.ResponsibilitiesTeachingTeach one course per semester, reflecting a 1-1 teaching load.Offer undergraduate courses on freedom of speech and related topics.Develop a Free Speech Seminar within Bentley's Falcon Discovery Seminar first-year program.Foster rigorous, inclusive, and intellectually open classroom environments in which students can engage constructively with competing ideas and perspectives.Scholarship and External EngagementMaintain an active and visible research agenda related to free speech, free expression, or closely connected areas of inquiry.Publish in scholarly journals and public-facing venues.Present research and ideas at national and international conferences, public forums, and professional gatherings.Contribute to public conversations about free expression, academic freedom, and civil discourse through writing, speaking, media engagement, or related activities.Develop and sustain relationships with relevant scholarly, professional, and civic organizations, which may include the Academic Freedom Alliance, Heterodox Academy, the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression, the American Association of University Professors, and the American Civil Liberties Union.Campus Engagement and the Bartlett InitiativeCollaborate closely with the Bartlett Chair of Free Enterprise on joint programming, including speaker series, public events, and curricular initiatives.Help shape and advance a compelling long-term vision for the Bartlett Initiative.Lead campus conversations on free expression, academic freedom, and civil discourse.Engage students and faculty in discussions about the role of free speech in higher education and democratic society.Serve as a resource to university leadership on issues of expression and academic freedom.Build connections between the Bartlett Initiative and relevant external scholars, organizations, and public conversations.Working with the Dean of Arts & Sciences and the Dean of Business, the Bartlett Chairs will jointly shape a visible and intellectually vibrant set of initiatives that connect free speech and free enterprise as foundations of liberal education.Bentley is committed to the teacher-scholar model, in which teaching, scholarship, service, and community engagement are valued. Bentley values intellectual diversity alongside diversity of background and experience and seeks faculty who can contribute to a culture of open inquiry, free expression, mutual respect, and constructive engagement across differences in viewpoint.Bentley University, located in suburban Boston, is an AACSB and NECHE accredited institution that enrolls approximately 5,500 students at the undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral levels. Bentley is ranked at or near the top in several categories by US News & World Report, including Best Regional Universities North and Most Innovative Schools, with Bloomberg ranking Bentley in the top 20 undergraduate business programs. Bentley's high graduation and retention rates and top-ranked Pulsifer Career Center reflect a commitment to student success and inclusiveness. With a strong faculty of teacher-scholars, Bentley strives to be a "Force for Good" through the integration of business with the arts and sciences, and a strong emphasis on ethics and social responsibility. Providing a stimulating academic community for faculty, staff, and students, Bentley supports its faculty as they pursue cutting-edge research and bring their expertise and real world understanding into the classroom.Application MaterialsApplicants should submit:An up-to-date curriculum vitae.A letter of interest that:Describes the candidate's qualifications for the Bartlett Chair of Free Speech.Explains the direct and substantive relationship of the candidate's scholarship, teaching, public engagement, or professional activities to the value and principles of free speech.Outlines the candidate's vision or ideas for advancing the Bartlett Initiative through programming, teaching, scholarship, external engagement, and campus dialogue.A teaching statement that includes a description of how the candidate has demonstrated, or intends to create and support, an inclusive and intellectually open classroom environment.A teaching portfolio that includes sample syllabi and available student and/or peer evaluations.Up to five scholarly works that the candidate wishes the committee to emphasize when evaluating their research and scholarship.The names and contact information of three references. Bentley will contact these individuals confidentially only for candidates who advance in the search process.Application Deadline: For full consideration, applications should be submitted by November 1, 2026. Review will continue until the position is filled.Pay TransparencyAt Bentley we offer a "total rewards" package designed to attract, motivate, retain, and reward our employees. This includes competitive compensation, robust benefits, career development and opportunities, generous paid time off, workplace flexibility and a positive, engaging employee experience. In alignment with the Massachusetts Pay Transparency Act and our commitment to equity and transparency, we're sharing the salary grade range for this role. The grade range is based on market data and the scope of responsibilities. Final pay will depend on your experience, education, home department, and other relevant qualifications.Professor Rank Range: $127,000 - $165,000Associate Professor Rank Range: $110,000 - $145,000If you have questions about the salary grade range or need additional information, please contact us at[email protected].Bentley University requires references checks and may conduct other pre-employment screening.DIVERSITY STATEMENTBentley University strives to create a campus community that welcomes the exchange of ideas, and fosters a culture that values differences and views them as a strength in our community.Bentley University is an Equal Opportunity Employer, building strength through diversity. The University is committed to building a community of talented students, faculty and staff who reflect the diversity of global business. We strongly encourage applications from persons from underrepresented groups, individuals with disabilities, covered veterans and those with diverse experiences and backgrounds.Apply Here:https://www.click2apply.net/qy5lqbC4A61GjC2eWUxKmaPI287144084

jobs.title: Postdoctoral researcher
jobs.description: The Chair of Metaphysics in the Faculty of Philosophy at LMU Munich invites applications for one postdoc position in a multi-university John Templeton Foundation supported project on the physics and philosophy of open quantum systems. This is a fixed term (non-tenure track) postdoctoral position that runs for two years. The starting date is January 15, 2027.The candidate will be expected to maintain an active research program in metaphysics and philosophy of physics, including issues related to the metaphysics of quantum open systems. They will also be expected to participate in the weekly group activities of the Chair of Metaphysics. The position will include some administrative tasks, such as the organization of workshops.
jobs.instructions:
Applications should be written entirely in English and include the following:
letter of interest, CV with certificates, writing sample, research plan (maximum two pages), the names and e-mail addresses of three professors who can send letters of recommendation, if requested.
These materials should be compiled into a single PDF and sent by October 15, 2026 at the latest to:[email protected]. The e-mail subject line should include "JTF postdoc application" and the applicant's name. Applicants should hold a PhD in philosophy at the time of application.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Philosophy
jobs.description: Assistant Professor of PhilosophyIllinois Wesleyan University invites applications for the position of Assistant Professor of Philosophy (Tenure Track). The start date for this position is August 15, 2027.  Area of Specialization: Open. Area of Competence: Philosophy of Science, broadly construed.The successful candidate should have a strong commitment to excellence in undergraduate education and have earned a PhD in Philosophy or a closely related field by August 1, 2027. In addition to philosophy of science, the candidate will be expected to teach introductory logic.  The curriculum also has needs in philosophy of feminism, mind, and race, and candidates are encouraged to indicate teaching interest and ability in any of these areas.  Candidates who are able to broaden the curriculum, including through contributions to interdisciplinary programs and the shared curriculum, are also welcome to apply.Responsibilities of Tenure-Track Faculty:6-course teaching load per yearAcademic advising in the disciplineScholarly (or artistic) achievementDepartmental and University serviceAbout the Tenure Track:  At Illinois Wesleyan, Tenure-Track faculty engage students through six teaching assignments each year, pursue productive scholarly or artistic work, serve as academic advisors, and engage in departmental and campus-wide service.  After receiving feedback on formative reviews in the second, third, and fourth years of employment, a case for tenure and promotion is submitted in the fall of the sixth year.Tenure-track faculty are eligible for sabbatical following six complete academic years of full-time service and every seven years thereafter. Additionalprofessional developmentopportunities include the possibility of start-up funds, the potential for junior faculty leave, andsupport for the development of external grants. The Thorpe Center for Curricular and Faculty Development supports faculty in their teaching and scholarly or artistic work including peer-to-peer mentoring, workshops, internal grants, and assistance with instructional design and technology.About IWU:  Founded in 1850, Illinois Wesleyan University is a nationally ranked, small, private undergraduate liberal arts university with highly selective admission criteria and a tradition of teaching excellence emphasizing the integration of the liberal arts and professional education. We are located in Bloomington, IL, a metro area of 170,000 people, which is about a two or three hour drive from Chicago, St. Louis, and Indianapolis. We are strongly committed to fostering an environment that values varied perspectives and backgrounds.Application Information:  Please submit the following to IWU Department of Philosophy Administrative Specialist, Amy Aldeman, at[email protected]:Cover letter addressing qualifications for the position, including experience with and commitment to fostering an inclusive learning environment at a primarily undergraduate levelCurriculum vitaeWriting sampleTeaching portfolio (including teaching statement and sample syllabi)Three letters of recommendationFurther materials may be requested by the search committee.Questions regarding the position may be directed to IWU Philosophy Department Chair Andy Engen at[email protected].Review of applications will begin November 2, 2026, and continue until the position has been filled.Compensation and Benefits:Nine-month appointmentSalary Range: $55-60K, and based on experienceThe final candidate will pass a pre-employment background investigation.An overview of IWU benefits can be foundhere.Illinois Wesleyan University may offer H-1B or other work authorization visa sponsorship for this position. Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of hire and maintain work authorization throughout the employment term.Illinois Wesleyan University is committed to recruiting, supporting, and fostering a community that values a wide range of perspectives and backgrounds among our outstanding faculty, staff, and students. We seek candidates who have a demonstrated commitment to contributing to and enhancing our community in these areas. Illinois Wesleyan University is an equal opportunity employer dedicated to promoting excellence through a variety of viewpoints; details athttps://www.iwu.edu/about/non-discrimination.html.

jobs.institution: Department of Philosophy, University of Florida
jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Philosophy
jobs.description: The Department of Philosophy at the University of Florida, College of Liberal Arts and Sciences, invites applications for a nine-month, full-time, tenure-accruing position at the rank of Assistant Professor beginning August 16, 2027, in the History of Modern Philosophy.The successful candidate will pursue an active research agenda in Early Modern Philosophy and provide service to the department, the university, and the profession. Although candidates must have Early Modern Philosophy as their core area of research, additional expertise in either Medieval Philosophy or 19th-Century Philosophy would be useful as the department has teaching needs in all these areas. Tenure-line faculty are typically assigned four courses per academic year at the undergraduate and graduate levels. In addition to regularly teaching required courses for the undergraduate Philosophy major and minor, the ability to contribute significantly to graduate education and the mentoring of graduate students will also be expected.The department has recently grown with multiple hires in the last several years and currently has a significant number of faculty working primarily in the history of philosophy. It is committed to ensuring a robust coverage of all the core areas of philosophy, though it has developed special strength in the ethics of technology and the philosophy of artificial intelligence. The department also has a good working relationship with the newly established Hamilton School for Classical and Civic Education, which has hired several faculty members with interests in the history of philosophy during the past few years. To learn more about the Department of Philosophy, applicants are encouraged to visit the departmental website (Department of Philosophy).
jobs.instructions:
For full consideration, applications must be submitted online by the posted deadline of November 30, 2026.

A complete application includes:
•	Letter of application summarizing the applicant's qualifications, interests, and suitability for the position
•	A complete curriculum vitae
•	A statement regarding the applicant’s research agenda
•	A statement and supporting materials regarding teaching effectiveness
•	A sample of written work of moderate length
•	Names and contact information for three professional references 

Application must be submitted by 11:55 p.m. (ET) of the posting end date. Review of applications will begin on December 1, 2026, and will continue until a successful applicant is selected.

All candidates for employment are subject to a pre-employment screening which includes a review of criminal records, reference checks, and verification of education.

The selected candidate will be required to provide an official transcript to the hiring department upon hire. A transcript will not be considered “official” if a designation of “Issued to Student” is visible. Degrees earned from an educational institution outside of the United States require evaluation by a professional credentialing service provider approved by the National Association of Credential Evaluation Services (NACES), which can be found at http://www.naces.org/.

jobs.description: University of California, DavisAssistant Professor of Philosophy and LinguisticsThe Departments of Philosophy and Linguistics at the University of California, Davis invite applications for a joint tenure-track position at the rank of Assistant Professor, specializing in research questions at the intersection of philosophy of language and theoretical/computational linguistics. A successful candidate is expected to be active in both departments. The anticipated start date is July 1, 2027.We seek a scholar whose research and teaching bridge philosophy, linguistics, and modern computational methods, including formal (symbolic) models, neural language models, and other formal or computational systems. We welcome candidates working on areas such as: semantics and pragmatics, morphology and syntax of natural languages, philosophy of linguistics, language evolution and change, AI interpretability or alignment, and computational models of communication. We are especially interested in candidates whose work addresses how meaning, reasoning, linguistic structure, or grammar is represented and processed in generative AI systems.The successful candidate will hold a joint appointment in the Department of Philosophy and the Department of Linguistics and will be expected to develop a robust, externally fundable research program alongside a strong record of teaching and mentorship at both the undergraduate and graduate levels. The successful candidate will contribute to core curricula in both departments, and the Cognitive Science program. Applicants must hold a Ph.D. in Philosophy, Linguistics, Cognitive Science, Computer Science, or a closely related field by the start of the appointment. Candidates should demonstrate strong potential for excellence in research and teaching at the intersection of philosophy, linguistics, and computational/AI methods.Applicants should submit: curriculum vitae, a cover letter that clearly states reasons for the candidate’s interest in the position, qualifications, and a summary of academic trajectory; statements of research and teaching interests, official graduate transcripts, one writing sample (publication, submitted manuscript, or dissertation chapter), and three letters of recommendation through the online application system found at: https://recruit.ucdavis.edu/JPF07874.This recruitment is conducted at the Assistant rank. The resulting hire will be at the Assistant rank, regardless of the proposed appointee’s qualifications. Appointment level and salary are commensurate with experience. A reasonable estimate for this position is $117,000 to $143,700. The position will remain open until filled. Applications received by November 15, 2026 will receive full initial consideration. The University of California, Davis, is an affirmative action/equal opportunity employer with a strong institutional commitment to the achievement of diversity among its faculty and staff.

jobs.description: POSITION DESCRIPTIONThe Department of Philosophy at theUniversity of Toronto Mississauga (UTM) invites applications for a full-time tenure stream position in Ethics and/or Social and Political Philosophy. The appointment will be at the rank of Assistant Professor, with an anticipated start date of July 1, 2027.REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONSCandidates must have earned a PhD degree in Philosophy or a closely related area by the time of appointment, or shortly thereafter, with a demonstrated record of excellence in research and teaching in Ethics and/or Social and Political Philosophy. The capacity to teach Feminist Philosophy is an asset for this position. We seek candidates whose research and teaching interests complement and enhance ourexisting departmental strengths.Candidates must provide evidence of research excellence which can be demonstrated through a record of publications in top-ranked and field-relevant journals or forthcoming publications that meet high international standards; the submitted research dossier; presentations at significant conferences; awards and accolades; and strong endorsements from referees.Evidence of excellence in teaching will be demonstrated through teaching accomplishments, the teaching dossier (including the required materials outlined below), and strong letters of reference.RESPONSIBILITIESThe successful candidate will be expected to pursue innovative and independent research and to establish an outstanding, competitive, and externally funded research program.In addition, the successful candidate will be assigned a teaching and service load. The successful candidate must be able to teach a wide range of courses in philosophy from the introductory to advanced levels, including both undergraduate and graduate courses. Undergraduate classes will be taught at the University of Toronto Mississauga campus, and graduate courses at the tri-campus Graduate Department of Philosophy on the St. George campus. The successful candidate will also be expected to participate in the regular supervision of graduate students in thetri-campus Graduate Department of Philosophy.HIRING SALARY RANGEThe expected salary range is $130,000 to $150,000 CAD per annum, depending on experience. Negotiations beyond this salary range will be considered for exceptionally qualified candidates.ABOUT USThe University of Toronto has three campuses, St. George, Scarborough, and Mississauga, each with its own Department of Philosophy offering undergraduate programs. The advertised position is at the Mississauga Campus. The Graduate Department of Philosophyat the University of Toronto is a tri-campus department, consisting of philosophy faculty appointed on all three campuses. Graduate teaching and supervision typically take place on the St. George campus.The Tri-Campus Graduate Department of Philosophy at the University of Toronto is widely recognized as Canada’s best and most comprehensive philosophy department and as an international leader in the field. The University of Toronto offers the opportunity to teach, conduct research and live in one of the most diverse and cosmopolitan cities in the world.For more information about the Department of Philosophy at the University of Toronto Mississauga and the Tri-Campus Graduate Department of Philosophy please visit our website at www.philosophy.utoronto.ca.At UTM we are committed to fostering an environment of diversity and inclusion. With an enviably diverse student body, we especially welcome applications from candidates who identify as Indigenous, Black, or racially visible (persons of colour), and who have experience working with, teaching or mentoring diverse groups of students. Candidates must demonstrate, in their application materials, an ability to foster diversity on campus and within the curriculum or discipline, and must show evidence of a commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion, and the promotion of a respectful and collegial environment.Candidates should submit a statement describing their contributions to equity, diversity, and inclusion, which might cover topics such as (but not limited to): teaching that incorporates a focus on underrepresented communities; efforts undertaken to develop inclusive pedagogies, collaboration, and engagement with underrepresented communities; and mentoring of students from underrepresented groups. If you have questions about this statement, please contact Acting Chair Jennifer Nagel[email protected].APPLICATION PROCESSAll application materials, including recent reference letters, must be received byNovember 16, 2026.All qualified candidates are invited to apply online by clicking the link below. Your CV and cover letter should be uploaded into the dedicated fields. Please submitadditional application materials in PDF format only. Applicants must submit the following materials:a cover letter in a file labelled “ApplicantLastName cover letter.pdf”;a current curriculum vitae in a file labelled “ApplicantLastName CV.pdf”;a research dossier in a file labelled “ApplicantLastName research.pdf”,containing a statement outlining current and future research interests, and a recent piece of academic writing;a teaching dossier, including a teaching statement, sample course materials, and teaching evaluations, in a file labelled “ApplicantLastName teaching.pdf”;an equity, diversity, and inclusion statement (as noted above), in a file labelled “ApplicantLastName EDI statement.pdf”; andthe name and contact information of three references.Candidates may be asked for additional samples of writing later in the search process.The University of Toronto’s recruiting tool will automatically solicit and collect letters of reference from each referee within 48 hours of an application being submitted. Applicants remain responsible for ensuring that referees submit recent letters (on letterhead, dated, and signed) by the closing date. Submission guidelines and details on the automatic reference letter collection, including timelines, are available in the candidate FAQ.If you have any questions about this position, please contact Eden Finer[email protected].All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however, Canadians and permanent residents will be given priority.DIVERSITY STATEMENTThe University of Toronto embraces Diversity and is building a culture of belonging that increases our capacity to effectively address and serve the interests of our global community. We strongly encourage applications from Indigenous Peoples, Black and racialized persons, women, persons with disabilities, and people of diverse sexual and gender identities. We value applicants who have demonstrated a commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion and recognize that diverse perspectives, experiences, and expertise are essential to strengthening our academic mission.As part of your application, you will be asked to complete a brief Diversity Survey. This survey is voluntary. Any information directly related to you is confidential and cannot be accessed by search committees or human resources staff. The teaching load is 4-3. Faculty may also teach ASC-101: Thinking Through, a course required of all incoming students in the University's Foundations and Transformations general education program, in which each section is built around a pressing question chosen by the instructor. Faculty may also contribute to the department's Ethical Reasoning certificate and minor. We seek a colleague committed to excellent undergraduate teaching who maintains an active scholarly agenda appropriate to a teaching-focused institution.Widener is a metropolitan university in Chester, Pennsylvania, near Philadelphia. Many of our students are first-generation college students, and many are preparing for careers in nursing, business, engineering, and other professional fields. Philosophy courses at Widener, particularly logic and ethics, serve students across the university, most of whom are not philosophy majors. We are looking for a teacher who finds that work meaningful and knows how to reach students who did not arrive expecting to study philosophy.The Ph.D. in Philosophy or a closely related field is required by August 15, 2027.Widener University is committed to fostering an environment in which faculty, staff, and students from a variety of backgrounds, cultures, and personal experiences are welcomed and can thrive. jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Philosophy
jobs.aoc: Philosophy of Law (or a related philosophical area)
jobs.description: Stetson University seeks a broadly trained teacher-scholar with an area of competence in the philosophy of law or a related philosophical area with legal experience relevant to the position.This is a full-time, 9-month position beginning in August 2027.QUALIFICATIONS:A Ph.D. in Philosophy, or in a closely related field with substantial graduate preparation in philosophy, completed by August 2027. The successful candidate will have an active scholarly agenda and demonstrated excellence in teaching undergraduates. The University seeks a broadly trained teacher-scholar with an area of competence in the philosophy of law or a related philosophical area with legal experience relevant to the position. With respect to legal experience, a J.D. is preferred. However, candidates with comparable legal preparation or substantial professional experience in legal practice, courts, government, public-interest advocacy, mediation, regulatory or compliance work, or legal education will also receive full consideration. Experience with pre-law advising, LSAT preparation, or coaching Mock Trial or Moot Court is welcome but not required. The ability to teach Introduction to Logic is also desirable.RESPONSIBILITIES:The annual teaching load includes five regular courses and one student-centered immersive experience (equivalent to one course) as a part of the University’s experiential, contemporary, and integrative learning initiative – Hatter Ready. Teaching responsibilities will include introductory and advanced courses in the candidate’s areas of competence, regular contributions to law-related undergraduate programming, and courses in Stetson’s General Education curriculum. Depending on the candidate’s expertise, courses might include Philosophy of Law, Political Philosophy, constitutionalism, theories of rights and justice, legal reasoning and interpretation, or other philosophically informed courses concerning law and legal institutions. The successful candidate will also help strengthen connections among the Philosophy Department, the Law Ready curriculum, Stetson’s broader pre-law programming, and Stetson’s College of Law.For more information on our expectations in teaching and scholarship, our tenure policies, and our support for faculty development, please see the Academic Affairs website at https://www.stetson.edu/administration/provost/prospective-faculty/index.php.The successful candidate will contribute to Stetson’s growing Law Ready undergraduate curriculum, which serves approximately 300 students interested in attending law school. Law Ready brings together interdisciplinary coursework, the Law, Society, and Advocacy and Business Law minors, a living-learning community, pre-law advising, and experiential opportunities such as Mock Trial and Moot Court. Stetson’s Mock Trial team is currently ranked number one in Florida, providing students with an exceptional opportunity to develop practical skills in trial advocacy alongside the excellence of Stetson Law’s trial-advocacy programs.Law Ready approaches preparation for law school through the liberal arts. We therefore seek a colleague who can help students develop the close reading, analytical reasoning, clear writing, oral advocacy, ethical reflection, and understanding of legal institutions needed for success in law school and civic life. The successful candidate should be prepared to engage students seriously and respectfully with competing positions on contested legal, moral, and political questions.THE DEPARTMENT:Stetson’s Department of Philosophy takes a rigorous, interdisciplinary, and pluralistic approach to undergraduate liberal arts education. The successful candidate will join a close-knit department as its third full-time faculty member. Our faculty are active scholars with strong publication records and wide-ranging interests in analytic, continental, feminist, historical, experimental, and applied philosophy. We work deliberately to create a welcoming intellectual home for philosophy students through close mentoring, undergraduate research, and immersive activities such as Philosophy Club, Idle Talk, and a Film Club. The department is also closely connected to Stetson’s expanding pre-law initiatives: its chair currently serves as Pre-Law Director for the University’s Law Ready program.THE COLLEGE OF ARTS AND SCIENCES:Stetson’s College of Arts and Sciences (https://www.stetson.edu/artsci/) is the largest and most diverse of the University’s colleges and schools; it includes the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, education, and creative arts. With nineteen academic departments and nine interdisciplinary programs, the College is the liberal arts core of the University. A great strength of the College is its faculty of approximately 140 full-time teacher-scholars. The College offers 31 undergraduate majors and 34 undergraduate minors; seven graduate degrees are offered in Education, Counselor Education, and Creative Writing. Every undergraduate major requires a senior research project, allowing students the opportunity to design and carry out independent research under faculty mentorship. Our academic programs are shaped by the values of social justice and civic responsibility. All of our courses and programs of study promote engaged learning, whereby students create connections between the classroom or lab and the local, regional, and global community. The academic programs of the College of Arts and Sciences prepare students to live significant lives, to interact with and positively affect the world around them.THE UNIVERSITY:Founded in 1883, Stetson University (http://www.stetson.edu) is a private, selective university comprised of a rich array of liberal arts and professional academic programs. Collectively, Stetson’s faculty works with approximately 3,700 students in undergraduate, graduate, and professional programs. The University’s historic main campus, located in DeLand, enrolls approximately 2,300 students in undergraduate programs in the College of Arts and Sciences, the School of Business Administration, and the School of Music. Stetson University College of Law, Florida’s first law school, moved from the main campus to Gulfport in 1954, and, with the addition of the Tampa Law Center, serves approximately 1,000 students working full-time or part-time toward J.D. or LL.M. degrees. Graduate programs based at the main campus in DeLand include Business, Accounting, Education, Counseling, and Creative Writing, with Educational Leadership cohorts also offered at the Gulfport campus. Stetson is Florida’s oldest private institution of higher learning and was the first private college in Florida to be granted a chapter of Phi Beta Kappa.Stetson University provides an inspiring education that engages students with rigorous academic and creative study grounded in liberal learning and promotes civic values of personal and social responsibility. Working closely with faculty and with one another, students cultivate abilities to explore issues deeply, think critically, reason empirically, speak persuasively, and connect ideas creatively. Firmly committed to inclusive excellence, our vibrant community of teacher-scholars nurtures the potential of individual students to lead lives of significance and prepares each to meet the challenges of shaping the future—locally, nationally, and globally.THE COMMUNITY:DeLand is a picturesque residential community of 38,000 located 20 miles west of Daytona Beach and 35 miles northeast of Orlando. The area offers extensive cultural as well as recreational activities.SALARY:Salary is competitive.STARTING DATE: August 9, 2027.APPLICATION:Applicants are asked to supply:a cover letter that includes a statement about the candidate’s teaching and research interests, experience relevant to the position, and a discussion of how the candidate proposes to develop as a teacher-scholara teaching portfolio, inclusive of teaching philosophy, sample syllabi (classes taught or that you would like to teach), and student evaluations for courses taught (where available)a curriculum vitaethe names, addresses, e-mail addresses, and telephone numbers of three professional references to be contacted later in the processIn the cover letter, candidates are encouraged to highlight skills and experiences that demonstrate a commitment to promoting inclusive academic environments and engaging across differences.Please visit our Career Opportunities Website (https://www.schooljobs.com/careers/stetson/delandfaculty?) to apply and to upload your application documents.Review of applications will begin on November 1, 2026, and continue until the position is filled.WORK AUTHORIZATION REQUIREMENTS:Work authorization sponsorship may be available for this position. However, sponsorship is contingent upon the non-applicability of the visa petition fees outlined in the relevant Executive Order. International candidates are encouraged to apply, but should be aware that eligibility for sponsorship will be evaluated in accordance with current U.S. immigration regulations and institutional policies.Stetson University is an Equal Opportunity Employer that affirms inclusive environments and engaging across differences as a core value of academic excellence in which all employees and candidates are treated equally no matter their age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, genetic information, marital status, military status, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, or shared ancestry. We are committed to achieving equal access in education, employment, and participation through the recruitment and retention of outstanding faculty, staff, and students from a tapestry of backgrounds, and to meaningful academic and intellectual transformation in curriculum, research and service.We are dedicated to actions and policies that foster a community in which individuals across all identities, cultures, backgrounds, and viewpoints work together to create opportunities for engagement through rewarding and fulfilling careers and personal experiences in an increasingly diverse society and a globalized world. We encourage qualified candidates across all backgrounds and identities to apply for employment.  Stetson University is an EEO, ADA, ADEA, and GINA employer.

jobs.description: Director, McCourtney Institute for Democracy, and Associate Professor/Professor in the College of the Liberal Arts, Penn StatePOSITION SPECIFICSThe Pennsylvania State University, College of the Liberal Arts, in University Park, PA, USA, invites applications for the position of Director of the https://democracy.psu.edu/, which will be filled at the rank of Associate Professor or Professor with tenure within an appropriate academic department within the College. The anticipated start date is Fall 2027, with flexibility.The McCourtney Institute for Democracy promotes scholarship and practical innovations to understand, preserve, and advance democracy. Through research, teaching, and public outreach, the Institute leverages the resources of Penn State and the College of the Liberal Arts to conduct research on democracy and society, defend democratic practices, and foster democratic citizenship and educate for democratic engagement.Some of the regular activities of the Center include awarding the Brown Democracy Medal annually, publishing the Podcast “Democracy Works,” providing funding to support for faculty and student research, recruiting students in the Nevins Fellows program, and connecting with other institutions studying democracy. The institute supports two research centers, the Center for Democratic Deliberation and the Center for Research on Democratic Resilience.We seek a thoughtful Director who will lead the Center administratively and intellectually by supporting rigorous research on democracy, expanding the connections and research activities of the Center around campus, devising new research and outreach initiatives, engaging alumni to support the Center, growing the community of scholars engaged with the Center, and maintaining current signature activities. The Director manages four Institute staff (the managing director, communications specialist, podcast group manager, and administrative assistant).The Director will be expected to maintain an active research agenda and to be part of their academic unit and disciplinary community. A teaching release and supplement will be provided during the successful candidate's term as Director.Candidates for the Director of the Institute (Associate Professor rank) must have demonstrated excellence as a researcher, scholar, and teacher in a relevant field and have an established reputation in scholarly achievement. Duties will involve a combination of teaching, research, and service, based on the candidate's qualifications.Candidates for the Director of the Institute (Professor rank) must have demonstrated excellence as a researcher, scholar, and teacher in a relevant field, and evidence of a substantial record of advanced research as well as leadership in their field of specialization. Duties will involve a combination of teaching, research, and service, based on the candidate's qualifications.Qualified applicants for both ranks will have a Ph.D. in a relevant humanities or social science discipline by date of appointment.For both ranks, an applicant's research should align with the Institute's interest in promoting research and knowledge about democracy in the United States or global context, broadly defined. Candidates should have an excellent publication record in their field; a commitment to securing external funding; a commitment to working with alumni and development; and a track record of excellence in teaching, mentoring, and academic service. Successful candidates must demonstrate experience in developing and maintaining institutionally sustainable research centers or other initiatives, and the ability to productively engage and support the research of scholars from other disciplines.Applicants must apply online at https://hr.psu.edu/careers and should include a cover letter, a curriculum vitae, and a list of three references. In the cover letter, applicants should discuss their experience in managing, creating, or supervising academic programs or research centers, as well as in pursuing external funding. They should also discuss their vision of a research center centered around the mission described above.We will request letters of recommendation and teaching materials from candidates who advance in the search process. Review of applications will begin October 15, 2026, and will continue until the position has been filled.Please direct questions about the process via email to one of the committee co-chairs (Scott Bennett, Senior Associate Dean for Research and Graduate Studies, mailto:[email protected]; Amy Allen, Associate Dean for Faculty Affairs and Advancement, mailto:[email protected]).BACKGROUND CHECKS/CLEARANCESEmployment with the University will require successful completion of background check(s) in accordance with University policies.BENEFITSPenn State provides a competitive benefits package for full-time employees designed to support both personal and professional wellbeing. In addition to comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, employees enjoy robust retirement plans. One of the standout benefits is the generous 75% tuition discount, available to employees as well as eligible spouses and children.For more detailed information, please visit our https://hr.psu.edu/current-employee/benefits (Note: For Postdoctoral benefits, please see our https://hr.psu.edu/current-employee/benefits/post-doc-appts page.)CAMPUS SECURITY CRIME STATISTICSPursuant to the Jeanne Clery Disclosure of Campus Security Policy and Campus Crime Statistics Act and the Pennsylvania Act of 1988, Penn State publishes a combined Annual Security and Annual Fire Safety Report (ASR). The ASR includes crime statistics and institutional policies concerning campus security, such as those concerning alcohol and drug use, crime prevention, the reporting of crimes, sexual assault, and other matters. The ASR is available for review https://police.psu.edu/annual-security-reports.EEO IS THE LAWPenn State is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to providing employment opportunities to all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status. If you are unable to use our online application process due to an impairment or disability, please contact 814-865-1473.Penn State is committed to and accountable for advancing equity, respect, and belonging. We embrace individual uniqueness, as well as a culture of belonging that supports equity initiatives, leverages the educational and institutional benefits of inclusion in society, and provides opportunities for engagement intended to help all members of the community thrive. We value belonging as a core strength and an essential element of the university's teaching, research, and service mission.To apply, visit https://psu.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/PSU_Academic/job/Penn-State-University-Park/Director--McCourtney-Institute-for-Democracy--and-Associate-Professor-Professor-in-the-College-of-the-Liberal-Arts--Penn-State_REQ_0000082100-1je-7b6743e818c64101b9c8f1e1a83abe11

jobs.institution: Philosophy Program, Resolution
jobs.title: Research Scientist
jobs.description: About the Philosophy Program at ResolutionWork on AI alignment raises philosophical questions, including what concepts like honesty mean, what character is, what moral competence looks like, which moral theories should guide model behavior, and what research ought (or ought not) be delegated to models. Resolution’s philosophy team seeks to advance alignment by examining these kinds of questions and testing empirical claims where experimentation can help. Some projects will be primarily conceptual; others will involve collaboration with empirical researchers.Our initial research agenda is under development. The following gives a flavor of the areas of research we are considering:Conceptual engineering.Alignment research depends on concepts such as honesty, harm, autonomy, and deference, each of which carries multiple senses in ordinary language. We want to understand what it means for a model to represent or operationalize one sense rather than another; how that representation can be changed through training data, context, or other interventions; and which version of a concept(s) a model should employ in a given setting. The goal is to characterize alignment-relevant concepts precisely enough to inform training targets, experimental hypotheses, and evaluation criteria.Character, traits, and constitutions.AI developers increasingly attempt to align models by shaping their character rather than specifying comprehensive sets of rules. But the underlying notions, including trait, persona, disposition, and character, remain poorly understood. We want to clarify the relationships among these concepts; determine which, if any, provides the right unit of analysis for alignment targets; investigate which traits advanced systems should possess; and study how those traits persist, generalize, and interact across contexts.Normative evaluation of models.What would moral competence in a model consist in? Does it require distinctive capacities, or does it emerge from more general forms of conceptual and practical competence? We want to design experiments that clarify how models make normative judgments and develop evidential standards for determining when, and in which contexts, reliance on those judgments may be warranted.Moral theories and alignment.Alignment methods presuppose some normative commitments and assumptions. These assumptions can enter system design through objectives, constitutions, training examples, or evaluation criteria. Sometimes, an explicit commitment to some moral theory is made in model development. Systems shaped by different normative frameworks may behave similarly at current capability levels while diverging substantially as their capabilities increase. We want to understand how different normative structures and moral theories are instantiated in AI systems, and what evidence could help us compare their likely alignment properties as capabilities improve.Epistemic and safety risks of automating conceptual reasoning.Conceptual reasoning work is increasingly being delegated to models, including within alignment research itself. It's an open question whether this should happen at all, and, if so, where the limits should be. We want to map the risks and help determine which forms of conceptual work can be delegated, under what conditions, and with what forms of oversight. We are also interested in methods for validating model-generated conceptual work, and in the scientific norms and evidential standards that can help govern AI-assisted alignment research.We are also interested in proposals for new philosophical research that could improve our understanding of alignment or alter how alignment research is conducted.About the roleThe team is new, and the people we hire now will play a significant role in shaping what it becomes. We are hiring research scientists across multiple levels. The scope of the role will depend on the candidate’s experience, research interests, and level of seniority.Research scientists may:Lead or contribute to original research projects in philosophy and AI alignment.Identify important but underspecified problems and turn them into projects.Connect philosophical analysis to empirical hypotheses, experimental designs, training approaches, or evaluation methods.Collaborate closely with researchers from machine learning and other relevant disciplines.Communicate research clearly through papers, internal reports, presentations, and external engagement.Contribute to the intellectual culture and development of the philosophy team and Resolution.Depending on seniority, research scientists may also:Define and lead broad or ambiguous areas of research.Help set the team’s research agenda and strategic priorities.Initiate and lead collaborations across Resolution and with external researchers.Supervise, mentor, or manage more junior researchers.Represent the philosophy team in organization-wide research planning.What we’re looking forYou may be a good fit if you:Hold a PhD in a relevant field, such as philosophy, cognitive science, psychology, mathematics, or machine learning, or have a record of rigorous research experience.Can demonstrate your motivation to work on AI alignment, including through previous publications in the field, relevant experiences, or a clear explanation of why you are pivoting your research focus to alignment.Can identify important questions in areas where the problems, concepts, or success criteria remain unclear.Are interested in connecting philosophical analysis with empirical research.Can communicate clearly and collaborate productively with researchers from different disciplinary backgrounds.We are particularly interested in candidates who have one or more of the following:Research experience in AI safety, AI alignment, or other domains relevant to making AI futures go well.The ability to design, run, or help develop experiments.Previous experience working in interdisciplinary research teams.The interest and capacity to translate conceptual questions into hypotheses, interventions, or evaluation criteria.Relevant expertise in areas such as epistemology, philosophy of science, philosophy of language, philosophy of mind, action theory, moral psychology, or ethics.You do not need to meet all of these criteria. If you are uncertain whether your background fits, we encourage you to apply.

jobs.description: Call for application: 4-yearpostdocposition in philosophy, University of ZurichYour responsibilitiesThe postdoc researcher will work in the Department of Philosophy at the University of Zurich, under the supervision of Professor Miloud Belkoniene. They will join Professor Belkoniene’s research team as part of the SNSF Starting Grant project 'Understanding: Between Contents and Phenomena'. The postdoc researcher will also join the ZEGRa research group, which is based at the University of Zurich and directed by Professor Anne Meylan and Professor Belkoniene (https://zegra.ch/).SNSF Starting Grant projectThe project “Understanding: Between Contents and Phenomena” draws on tools from the philosophy of language, the philosophy of science, epistemology and moral philosophy to investigate the relationships between linguistic, empirical and moral understanding in light of the capacities that are responsible for their achievement. One of the project's main objectives is to show that the manner in which representations, such as explanations, must be grasped to achieve an understanding of certain phenomena depends on the very nature of the phenomena that these representations depict. In particular, that the cognitive engagement with representations required to understand empirical phenomena differs significantly from that required to understand normative phenomena, such as moral phenomena.A full description of the project can be found at:https://miloudbelkoniene.org/https://zegra.ch/projects/understanding-between-contents-and-phenomena/Your profilePhD in Philosophy, preferably with a specialization in Epistemology, Philosophy of Language or Philosophy of Science (The successful candidate is expected to have obtained their PhD by the time they take up the position).Strong publication record demonstrating scientific productivity.Excellent oral and written communication skills in English.Interest in carrying out and publishing research on some of the project’s topics. jobs.description: University of Gothenburg is now hiring aPhD candidate in practical philosophy, with a focus on economic ethics and/or environmental ethics. Economic ethics is the application of moral or political philosophy to critical issues in business organizations or the economic system. Environmental ethics is the application of moral or political philosophy to critical issues in the relationship between humans and non-human environmental systems. The research area should be understood broadly so as to include subtopics like business ethics, the political philosophy of markets, ethics of commodification, ethics of climate change or biodiversity, collective action problems, and the philosophy of (environmental) economics. Any applications related to these subfields are welcome.The PhD candidate will join theFinancial Ethics Research Groupin the Department of Philosophy, Linguistics and Theory of Science. The research group consists of philosophers and economists dedicated to ethical and political issues raised by money and finance (in the broadest sense). The group’s previous projects have been on topics such as sustainable business, ethical investment, banking for the poor, digital currencies, climate metrics, and the value of biodiversity. More specifically, the PhD candidate will be connected to the research programSustainable Finance Lab, which is a collaboration between several Swedish universities that is funded by Vinnova, Sweden’s innovation agency. The program explores various aspects of how to make markets and money into a positive force for sustainable development.The applicant must describe a more specific research question within the area above that they intend to explore. Some examples of potential research questions are:What moral duties do commercial firms or banks have to mitigate climate change?Do consumers have a duty to buy sustainable goods, or invest in sustainable firms?How should societal institutions (such as central banks or the monetary system) be set up to promote biodiversity?Is the state justified in coercing market participants to mitigate climate change?What is the relationship between sustainability and human rights?Are current conceptualizations of sustainability in terms of environmental, social and governance (ESG) criteria adequate?Please note that a PhD position in Sweden means full-time employment for four years. The University of Gothenburg has excellent employment benefits such as a generous pay, wellness time during working hours, compensation for medical visits, a base vacation of 28 days, and an occupational pension.Applications must be received by:October 13, 2026For more information, please visitUniversity of Gothenburg’s recruitment portal.

jobs.description: The Plunkett Centre for Ethics at the Australian Catholic University (ACU) is pleased to announce two PhD scholarships for research in bioethics. We are especially interested in topics related to flourishing in later lifehttps://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/hast.5022> or flourishing at the end of lifehttps://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11017-024-09679-x>, though we will be open to receiving applications in other areas.The Plunkett Centre is a philosophical bioethics centre and joint initiative of ACU and several partner organisations in the health and aged care sector. Founded in 1992, the Centre aims to advance ethical reflection on human health and wellbeing through research and teaching.Home to several recognised bioethicists and philosophers, the Centre has published extensively on the ethics of end-of-life care, clinical ethics, conscientious objection, reproductive technologies, and human flourishing at different life stages. Other interests of Plunkett faculty include artificial intelligence, moral psychology, ethics related to vulnerable medical groups (such as people living with dementia), philosophy of psychology, and the philosophy of memory.Successful applicants will receive the equivalent of a Research Training Program (RTP) Stipend, paid as a fortnightly stipend for up to 3.5 years. The PhD candidates will be based in the Plunkett Centre and successful candidates may be supervised by Plunkett Centre faculty, including Dr Xavier Symons, Dr Steve Matthews, Dr Bernadette Tobin, as well as affiliates and collaborators of the Centre. jobs.institution: Department of Philosophy, University of Helsinki
jobs.title: Postdoctoral Researcher/Researcher
jobs.description: We seek a researcher for a fixed term two-year position that runs from January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2028. The researcher will be a core member of the research team for the projectThe Many Faces of Inquiry: Towards a Dynamic and Pluralistic Epistemology. The project began in 2024 and will run until December 2029. It is funded by the Kone Foundation and is housed at the Philosophy unit at the University of Helsinki.ProjectFor us to be responsible epistemic agents, it does not suffice that we respond properly to the evidence that we happen to have. There are questions we should ask, facts we should consider, evidence that we should seek. There are both practical and epistemic norms that govern the (social or individual) practice of inquiry, and various kinds of aims that set standards of success for this process. The purpose of this research project is to contribute to developing a novel, principled, and systematic account of these norms and aims.What is the nature of the questions that initiate inquiry? What kind of answers fulfill the aims of inquiry? What kind of norms govern the questions and activity of inquiry, and what grounds their normative force for the subject? What kind of value do the answers have?The project team consists of the following members: Jaakko Hirvelä (epistemology), Antti Kauppinen (moral and political philosophy), Maria Lasonen (epistemology), Lilian O’Brien (philosophy of action), Ninni Suni (moral responsibility).ResponsibilitiesThe main task of the appointed researcher will be to conduct research on the central questions of the research project. They are expected to participate in project meetings, to contribute to the regular reading group of the project, and to attend research seminars held at the philosophy unit in Helsinki. The researcher will also help to organize conferences, seminars, and workshops, and assist in preparing new research proposals.Requirements for the position and assessment of qualificationsThe appointed researcher will hold a doctoral degree in philosophy and have an ambitious research agenda on topics relevant to the project. Applicants must have strong philosophical writing skills and excellent command of written and spoken English. When assessing applicants’ qualifications, particular attention will be paid to high-quality peer-reviewed publications and the quality of the research proposal.What we offerThe philosophy unit at Helsinki is home to several research projects on related topics and provides a vibrant and supportive research community. There are no teaching responsibilities with this position but there will be teaching opportunities. The salary for the position is paid by a grant from the Kone Foundation. The gross monthly amount, much of which is tax-free, ranges between 3,200 Euro and 3,800 Euro.Further information about the position can be obtained from Lilian O’Brien:[email protected].A diverse and equitable study and work culture is important to us. That is why we do our best to promote an inclusive university community. We encourage all qualified applicants from diverse backgrounds to apply for our positions.
jobs.instructions:
The application should consist of the following documents in English in PDF format:
(1) curriculum vitae (max 4 pages),
(2) a two-page research plan detailing their planned research for the project and how it connects with their previous work, and
(3) one writing sample (max 8000 words), and
(4) the name and contact information of one referee. 

Other attachments, including letters of recommendation or certificates, are not required at this point. We expect that you will send us a self-written application that reflects your own voice and thoughts. Applications generated by artificial intelligence do not meet our expectations.
Shortlisted candidates will be interviewed and final decisions will be made by November.
