The City College of New York has produced ten Nobel laureates.About the City College of New York Philosophy DepartmentThe Philosophy Department has nine full-time faculty members, 100 majors and 60 minors, an active Philosophy Club, and frequent departmental events, including the Philosophy Pizza Forum.Position DetailsThe Department of Philosophy at The City College of New York (CCNY) of the City University of New York (CUNY) invites applications for the Arthur Zitrin Professorship in Bioethics, an endowed position to be filled at the rank of Associate Professor, anticipated to begin in Fall 2027. The position will involve research, undergraduate teaching at the introductory level and in the applicant’s areas of expertise, and departmental service.The Zitrin Professorship will provide support of $10,000-$40,000 in addition to the salary range specified below, depending on experience and qualifications.Area of Specialization:BioethicsArea of Competence:OpenQUALIFICATIONSPh.D. in Philosophy.Evidence of excellence in research, teaching, and departmental service.PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONSPreferred but not required: experience in administering programs for students, such as internships, and/or experience with grants that could support such programs.COMPENSATIONSalary Range: $94,017-$113,745.  The Zitrin Professorship will provide support of $10,000-$40,000 in addition to the salary range, depending on experience and qualifications.CUNY offers faculty a competitive compensation and benefits package covering health insurance, pension and retirement benefits, paid parental leave, and savings programs. We also provide mentoring and support for research, scholarship, and publication as part of our commitment to ongoing faculty professional development.HOW TO APPLYOnly applications submitted through CUNYfirst will be considered for this position.If you are viewing this job posting in CUNYfirst, please click on "Apply Now" on the bottom of this page and follow the instructions.If you are viewing this job posting externally, please apply as follows:Go tohttps://cuny.jobs/Search for Job Opening ID number 32774Click on the "Apply Now" button and follow the instructions.Applications, including the following, must be uploaded to the CUNYfirst job application websiteas a single PDF document:1) Cover Letter;2) Curriculum Vitae;3) Summaries of recent student teaching evaluations;4) At least one article-length writing sample, and no more than three;5) Contact information (including email address) for at least three people willing to provide letters of recommendation.CLOSING DATENovember 15, 2026JOB SEARCH CATEGORYCUNY Job Posting: FacultyEQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITYCUNY encourages people with disabilities, minorities, veterans and women to apply.  At CUNY, Italian Americans are also included among our protected groups.  Applicants and employees will not be discriminated against on the basis of any legally protected category, including sexual orientation or gender identity. new_jobs.description: University of California, DavisAssistant Professor of Philosophy and LinguisticsThe Departments of Philosophy and Linguistics at the University of California, Davis invite applications for a joint tenure-track position at the rank of Assistant Professor, specializing in research questions at the intersection of philosophy of language and theoretical/computational linguistics. A successful candidate is expected to be active in both departments. The anticipated start date is July 1, 2027.We seek a scholar whose research and teaching bridge philosophy, linguistics, and modern computational methods, including formal (symbolic) models, neural language models, and other formal or computational systems. We welcome candidates working on areas such as: semantics and pragmatics, morphology and syntax of natural languages, philosophy of linguistics, language evolution and change, AI interpretability or alignment, and computational models of communication. We are especially interested in candidates whose work addresses how meaning, reasoning, linguistic structure, or grammar is represented and processed in generative AI systems.The successful candidate will hold a joint appointment in the Department of Philosophy and the Department of Linguistics and will be expected to develop a robust, externally fundable research program alongside a strong record of teaching and mentorship at both the undergraduate and graduate levels. The successful candidate will contribute to core curricula in both departments, and the Cognitive Science program. Applicants must hold a Ph.D. in Philosophy, Linguistics, Cognitive Science, Computer Science, or a closely related field by the start of the appointment. Candidates should demonstrate strong potential for excellence in research and teaching at the intersection of philosophy, linguistics, and computational/AI methods.Applicants should submit: curriculum vitae, a cover letter that clearly states reasons for the candidate’s interest in the position, qualifications, and a summary of academic trajectory; statements of research and teaching interests, official graduate transcripts, one writing sample (publication, submitted manuscript, or dissertation chapter), and three letters of recommendation through the online application system found at: https://recruit.ucdavis.edu/JPF07874.This recruitment is conducted at the Assistant rank. The resulting hire will be at the Assistant rank, regardless of the proposed appointee’s qualifications. Appointment level and salary are commensurate with experience. A reasonable estimate for this position is $117,000 to $143,700. The position will remain open until filled. Applications received by November 15, 2026 will receive full initial consideration. The University of California, Davis, is an affirmative action/equal opportunity employer with a strong institutional commitment to the achievement of diversity among its faculty and staff.

new_jobs.description: POSITION DESCRIPTIONThe Department of Philosophy at theUniversity of Toronto Mississauga (UTM) invites applications for a full-time tenure stream position in Ethics and/or Social and Political Philosophy. The appointment will be at the rank of Assistant Professor, with an anticipated start date of July 1, 2027.REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONSCandidates must have earned a PhD degree in Philosophy or a closely related area by the time of appointment, or shortly thereafter, with a demonstrated record of excellence in research and teaching in Ethics and/or Social and Political Philosophy. The capacity to teach Feminist Philosophy is an asset for this position. We seek candidates whose research and teaching interests complement and enhance ourexisting departmental strengths.Candidates must provide evidence of research excellence which can be demonstrated through a record of publications in top-ranked and field-relevant journals or forthcoming publications that meet high international standards; the submitted research dossier; presentations at significant conferences; awards and accolades; and strong endorsements from referees.Evidence of excellence in teaching will be demonstrated through teaching accomplishments, the teaching dossier (including the required materials outlined below), and strong letters of reference.RESPONSIBILITIESThe successful candidate will be expected to pursue innovative and independent research and to establish an outstanding, competitive, and externally funded research program.In addition, the successful candidate will be assigned a teaching and service load. The successful candidate must be able to teach a wide range of courses in philosophy from the introductory to advanced levels, including both undergraduate and graduate courses. Undergraduate classes will be taught at the University of Toronto Mississauga campus, and graduate courses at the tri-campus Graduate Department of Philosophy on the St. George campus. The successful candidate will also be expected to participate in the regular supervision of graduate students in thetri-campus Graduate Department of Philosophy.HIRING SALARY RANGEThe expected salary range is $130,000 to $150,000 CAD per annum, depending on experience. Negotiations beyond this salary range will be considered for exceptionally qualified candidates.ABOUT USThe University of Toronto has three campuses, St. George, Scarborough, and Mississauga, each with its own Department of Philosophy offering undergraduate programs. The advertised position is at the Mississauga Campus. The Graduate Department of Philosophyat the University of Toronto is a tri-campus department, consisting of philosophy faculty appointed on all three campuses. Graduate teaching and supervision typically take place on the St. George campus.The Tri-Campus Graduate Department of Philosophy at the University of Toronto is widely recognized as Canada’s best and most comprehensive philosophy department and as an international leader in the field. The University of Toronto offers the opportunity to teach, conduct research and live in one of the most diverse and cosmopolitan cities in the world.For more information about the Department of Philosophy at the University of Toronto Mississauga and the Tri-Campus Graduate Department of Philosophy please visit our website at www.philosophy.utoronto.ca.At UTM we are committed to fostering an environment of diversity and inclusion. With an enviably diverse student body, we especially welcome applications from candidates who identify as Indigenous, Black, or racially visible (persons of colour), and who have experience working with, teaching or mentoring diverse groups of students. Candidates must demonstrate, in their application materials, an ability to foster diversity on campus and within the curriculum or discipline, and must show evidence of a commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion, and the promotion of a respectful and collegial environment.Candidates should submit a statement describing their contributions to equity, diversity, and inclusion, which might cover topics such as (but not limited to): teaching that incorporates a focus on underrepresented communities; efforts undertaken to develop inclusive pedagogies, collaboration, and engagement with underrepresented communities; and mentoring of students from underrepresented groups. If you have questions about this statement, please contact Acting Chair Jennifer Nagel[email protected].APPLICATION PROCESSAll application materials, including recent reference letters, must be received byNovember 16, 2026.All qualified candidates are invited to apply online by clicking the link below. Your CV and cover letter should be uploaded into the dedicated fields. Please submitadditional application materials in PDF format only. Applicants must submit the following materials:a cover letter in a file labelled “ApplicantLastName cover letter.pdf”;a current curriculum vitae in a file labelled “ApplicantLastName CV.pdf”;a research dossier in a file labelled “ApplicantLastName research.pdf”,containing a statement outlining current and future research interests, and a recent piece of academic writing;a teaching dossier, including a teaching statement, sample course materials, and teaching evaluations, in a file labelled “ApplicantLastName teaching.pdf”;an equity, diversity, and inclusion statement (as noted above), in a file labelled “ApplicantLastName EDI statement.pdf”; andthe name and contact information of three references.Candidates may be asked for additional samples of writing later in the search process.The University of Toronto’s recruiting tool will automatically solicit and collect letters of reference from each referee within 48 hours of an application being submitted. Applicants remain responsible for ensuring that referees submit recent letters (on letterhead, dated, and signed) by the closing date. Submission guidelines and details on the automatic reference letter collection, including timelines, are available in the candidate FAQ.If you have any questions about this position, please contact Eden Finer[email protected].All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however, Canadians and permanent residents will be given priority.DIVERSITY STATEMENTThe University of Toronto embraces Diversity and is building a culture of belonging that increases our capacity to effectively address and serve the interests of our global community. We strongly encourage applications from Indigenous Peoples, Black and racialized persons, women, persons with disabilities, and people of diverse sexual and gender identities. We value applicants who have demonstrated a commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion and recognize that diverse perspectives, experiences, and expertise are essential to strengthening our academic mission.As part of your application, you will be asked to complete a brief Diversity Survey. This survey is voluntary. Any information directly related to you is confidential and cannot be accessed by search committees or human resources staff. Results will be aggregated for institutional planning purposes. For more information, please seehttp://uoft.me/UP.ACCESSIBILITY STATEMENTThe University strives to be an equitable and inclusive community, and proactively seeks to increase diversity among its community members. Our values regarding equity and diversity are linked with our unwavering commitment to excellence in the pursuit of our academic mission.The University is committed to the principles of the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA). As such, we strive to make our recruitment, assessment and selection processes as accessible as possible and provide accommodations as required for applicants with disabilities.If you require any accommodations at any point during the application and hiring process, please[email protected].

new_jobs.description: Reporting to the Dean of the College of Arts & Sciences, the Assistant Professor of Philosophy is a full-time tenure-track position beginning in Fall 2027.The Department of Philosophy in Widener University's College of Arts and Sciences invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Philosophy beginning in Fall 2027. The successful candidate must be prepared to teach Symbolic Logic (sentential and first-order predicate logic) and introductory ethics. The ability to teach business ethics is a plus. The teaching load is 4-3. It will include regular sections of Symbolic Logic and ethics courses serving the University's general education program, as well as courses in the candidate's areas of expertise. Faculty may also teach ASC-101: Thinking Through, a course required of all incoming students in the University's Foundations and Transformations general education program, in which each section is built around a pressing question chosen by the instructor. Faculty may also contribute to the department's Ethical Reasoning certificate and minor. We seek a colleague committed to excellent undergraduate teaching who maintains an active scholarly agenda appropriate to a teaching-focused institution.Widener is a metropolitan university in Chester, Pennsylvania, near Philadelphia. Many of our students are first-generation college students, and many are preparing for careers in nursing, business, engineering, and other professional fields. Philosophy courses at Widener, particularly logic and ethics, serve students across the university, most of whom are not philosophy majors. We are looking for a teacher who finds that work meaningful and knows how to reach students who did not arrive expecting to study philosophy.The Ph.D. in Philosophy or a closely related field is required by August 15, 2027.Widener University is committed to fostering an environment in which faculty, staff, and students from a variety of backgrounds, cultures, and personal experiences are welcomed and can thrive. The College of Arts and Sciences puts high priority on inclusive pedagogy, inclusive mentoring, and community engagement. Candidates who have experience working with a diverse range of faculty, staff, and students, or who would enjoy it, and who can contribute to a climate of inclusivity, are encouraged to identify their experiences in these areas throughout their application.To apply: Complete the online application form at widener.edu/jobs. Submit the following as a single PDF:A cover letter that addresses three items:Your preparation to teach Symbolic Logic (e.g., prior teaching or TA experience in formal logic, or graduate coursework).Your preparation to teach introductory ethics, and business ethics if applicable.Your current and planned scholarship.A CV.A statement of teaching philosophy.Evidence of teaching effectiveness, consisting at minimum of course evaluations, one sample syllabus, and one sample assignment.Incomplete applications will not be considered. Longlisted candidates will be asked to arrange for three confidential letters of reference and to provide graduate transcripts. First-round interviews will be conducted via Zoom. Review of applications will begin on November 2, 2026, and will continue until the position is filled.For more information about Widener University and the Department of Philosophy, seewww.widener.edu.DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES(including, but not limited to):Essential duties:TeachingThree or four classes a semester in Fall and Spring in area of expertise and/or first-year courses.ResearchEstablish and maintain a successful research program in the candidate’s field.Academic CitizenshipParticipate in departmental faculty meetings focused on departmental operations and planning and faculty development, including pedagogical strategies and student support initiatives.Participate in humanities division, college, and university meetings focused on faculty governance, curricular development, and enhancing campus-wide inclusive excellence.Secondary Responsibilities:Perform other job-related duties as assigned and participation in the intellectual life of the Department, the College of Arts & Sciences, and the University.MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS(education/training and experience required):Required:A demonstrated commitment to excellent undergraduate teaching, as shown in teaching materials and evaluations.Competence to teach symbolic logic through first-order predicate logic, as shown by prior teaching or TA experience in formal logic, or graduate coursework.Ability to teach introductory ethics.An active scholarly agenda appropriate to a teaching-focused institution.A Ph.D. in Philosophy or a closely related field by August 15, 2027.Preferred:Ability to teach business ethics.Interest in interdisciplinary teaching, including ASC-101: Thinking Through, the University's required first-year course, in which each section is organized around a pressing question chosen by the instructor.PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS AND/OR UNUSUAL HOURS:Must be available for in-person instruction.Must have the ability to speak clearly and audibly to deliver lectures, facilitate classroom discussions and interact with students and colleagues.All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply and will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, age, sex, sexual orientation, disability status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.  Widener University is committed to fostering an inclusive community in which faculty, staff, and students from a variety of backgrounds, cultures, and personal experiences are welcomed and can thrive. We are an equal opportunity employer and are committed to providing equal educational and employment opportunities for all persons without regard to age, color, national origin, race, religion, disability, veteran status, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, or status as a protected veteran.Some positions may be eligible for a hybrid or remote work arrangement that may include a partially or fully remote work location, consistent with Widener’s Flexible Work policy. U.S. work authorization is required.Widener University, an independent, metropolitan, doctoral-intensive university, connects curricula to social issues through civic engagement. Dynamic teaching, active scholarship, personal attention and experiential learning are key components of the Widener Experience. Located in Chester, PA, Widener's main campus is nestled between Philadelphia, PA and Wilmington, DE, with Law Schools located in both Harrisburg and Wilmington. For more information about the university, please visit our website atwww.widener.edu.

new_jobs.description: Stetson University seeks a broadly trained teacher-scholar with an area of competence in the philosophy of law or a related philosophical area with legal experience relevant to the position.This is a full-time, 9-month position beginning in August 2027.QUALIFICATIONS:A Ph.D. in Philosophy, or in a closely related field with substantial graduate preparation in philosophy, completed by August 2027. The successful candidate will have an active scholarly agenda and demonstrated excellence in teaching undergraduates. The University seeks a broadly trained teacher-scholar with an area of competence in the philosophy of law or a related philosophical area with legal experience relevant to the position. With respect to legal experience, a J.D. is preferred. However, candidates with comparable legal preparation or substantial professional experience in legal practice, courts, government, public-interest advocacy, mediation, regulatory or compliance work, or legal education will also receive full consideration. Experience with pre-law advising, LSAT preparation, or coaching Mock Trial or Moot Court is welcome but not required. The ability to teach Introduction to Logic is also desirable.RESPONSIBILITIES:The annual teaching load includes five regular courses and one student-centered immersive experience (equivalent to one course) as a part of the University’s experiential, contemporary, and integrative learning initiative – Hatter Ready. Teaching responsibilities will include introductory and advanced courses in the candidate’s areas of competence, regular contributions to law-related undergraduate programming, and courses in Stetson’s General Education curriculum. Depending on the candidate’s expertise, courses might include Philosophy of Law, Political Philosophy, constitutionalism, theories of rights and justice, legal reasoning and interpretation, or other philosophically informed courses concerning law and legal institutions. The successful candidate will also help strengthen connections among the Philosophy Department, the Law Ready curriculum, Stetson’s broader pre-law programming, and Stetson’s College of Law.For more information on our expectations in teaching and scholarship, our tenure policies, and our support for faculty development, please see the Academic Affairs website at https://www.stetson.edu/administration/provost/prospective-faculty/index.php.The successful candidate will contribute to Stetson’s growing Law Ready undergraduate curriculum, which serves approximately 300 students interested in attending law school. Law Ready brings together interdisciplinary coursework, the Law, Society, and Advocacy and Business Law minors, a living-learning community, pre-law advising, and experiential opportunities such as Mock Trial and Moot Court. Stetson’s Mock Trial team is currently ranked number one in Florida, providing students with an exceptional opportunity to develop practical skills in trial advocacy alongside the excellence of Stetson Law’s trial-advocacy programs.Law Ready approaches preparation for law school through the liberal arts. We therefore seek a colleague who can help students develop the close reading, analytical reasoning, clear writing, oral advocacy, ethical reflection, and understanding of legal institutions needed for success in law school and civic life. The successful candidate should be prepared to engage students seriously and respectfully with competing positions on contested legal, moral, and political questions.THE DEPARTMENT:Stetson’s Department of Philosophy takes a rigorous, interdisciplinary, and pluralistic approach to undergraduate liberal arts education. The successful candidate will join a close-knit department as its third full-time faculty member. Our faculty are active scholars with strong publication records and wide-ranging interests in analytic, continental, feminist, historical, experimental, and applied philosophy. We work deliberately to create a welcoming intellectual home for philosophy students through close mentoring, undergraduate research, and immersive activities such as Philosophy Club, Idle Talk, and a Film Club. The department is also closely connected to Stetson’s expanding pre-law initiatives: its chair currently serves as Pre-Law Director for the University’s Law Ready program.THE COLLEGE OF ARTS AND SCIENCES:Stetson’s College of Arts and Sciences (https://www.stetson.edu/artsci/) is the largest and most diverse of the University’s colleges and schools; it includes the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, education, and creative arts. With nineteen academic departments and nine interdisciplinary programs, the College is the liberal arts core of the University. A great strength of the College is its faculty of approximately 140 full-time teacher-scholars. The College offers 31 undergraduate majors and 34 undergraduate minors; seven graduate degrees are offered in Education, Counselor Education, and Creative Writing. Every undergraduate major requires a senior research project, allowing students the opportunity to design and carry out independent research under faculty mentorship. Our academic programs are shaped by the values of social justice and civic responsibility. All of our courses and programs of study promote engaged learning, whereby students create connections between the classroom or lab and the local, regional, and global community. The academic programs of the College of Arts and Sciences prepare students to live significant lives, to interact with and positively affect the world around them.THE UNIVERSITY:Founded in 1883, Stetson University (http://www.stetson.edu) is a private, selective university comprised of a rich array of liberal arts and professional academic programs. Collectively, Stetson’s faculty works with approximately 3,700 students in undergraduate, graduate, and professional programs. The University’s historic main campus, located in DeLand, enrolls approximately 2,300 students in undergraduate programs in the College of Arts and Sciences, the School of Business Administration, and the School of Music. Stetson University College of Law, Florida’s first law school, moved from the main campus to Gulfport in 1954, and, with the addition of the Tampa Law Center, serves approximately 1,000 students working full-time or part-time toward J.D. or LL.M. degrees. Graduate programs based at the main campus in DeLand include Business, Accounting, Education, Counseling, and Creative Writing, with Educational Leadership cohorts also offered at the Gulfport campus. Stetson is Florida’s oldest private institution of higher learning and was the first private college in Florida to be granted a chapter of Phi Beta Kappa.Stetson University provides an inspiring education that engages students with rigorous academic and creative study grounded in liberal learning and promotes civic values of personal and social responsibility. Working closely with faculty and with one another, students cultivate abilities to explore issues deeply, think critically, reason empirically, speak persuasively, and connect ideas creatively. Firmly committed to inclusive excellence, our vibrant community of teacher-scholars nurtures the potential of individual students to lead lives of significance and prepares each to meet the challenges of shaping the future—locally, nationally, and globally.THE COMMUNITY:DeLand is a picturesque residential community of 38,000 located 20 miles west of Daytona Beach and 35 miles northeast of Orlando. The area offers extensive cultural as well as recreational activities.SALARY:Salary is competitive.STARTING DATE: August 9, 2027.APPLICATION:Applicants are asked to supply:a cover letter that includes a statement about the candidate’s teaching and research interests, experience relevant to the position, and a discussion of how the candidate proposes to develop as a teacher-scholara teaching portfolio, inclusive of teaching philosophy, sample syllabi (classes taught or that you would like to teach), and student evaluations for courses taught (where available)a curriculum vitaethe names, addresses, e-mail addresses, and telephone numbers of three professional references to be contacted later in the processIn the cover letter, candidates are encouraged to highlight skills and experiences that demonstrate a commitment to promoting inclusive academic environments and engaging across differences.Please visit our Career Opportunities Website (https://www.schooljobs.com/careers/stetson/delandfaculty?) to apply and to upload your application documents.Review of applications will begin on November 1, 2026, and continue until the position is filled.WORK AUTHORIZATION REQUIREMENTS:Work authorization sponsorship may be available for this position. However, sponsorship is contingent upon the non-applicability of the visa petition fees outlined in the relevant Executive Order. International candidates are encouraged to apply, but should be aware that eligibility for sponsorship will be evaluated in accordance with current U.S. immigration regulations and institutional policies.Stetson University is an Equal Opportunity Employer that affirms inclusive environments and engaging across differences as a core value of academic excellence in which all employees and candidates are treated equally no matter their age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, genetic information, marital status, military status, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, or shared ancestry. We are committed to achieving equal access in education, employment, and participation through the recruitment and retention of outstanding faculty, staff, and students from a tapestry of backgrounds, and to meaningful academic and intellectual transformation in curriculum, research and service.We are dedicated to actions and policies that foster a community in which individuals across all identities, cultures, backgrounds, and viewpoints work together to create opportunities for engagement through rewarding and fulfilling careers and personal experiences in an increasingly diverse society and a globalized world. We encourage qualified candidates across all backgrounds and identities to apply for employment.  Stetson University is an EEO, ADA, ADEA, and GINA employer.

new_jobs.description: Director, McCourtney Institute for Democracy, and Associate Professor/Professor in the College of the Liberal Arts, Penn StatePOSITION SPECIFICSThe Pennsylvania State University, College of the Liberal Arts, in University Park, PA, USA, invites applications for the position of Director of the https://democracy.psu.edu/, which will be filled at the rank of Associate Professor or Professor with tenure within an appropriate academic department within the College. The anticipated start date is Fall 2027, with flexibility.The McCourtney Institute for Democracy promotes scholarship and practical innovations to understand, preserve, and advance democracy. Through research, teaching, and public outreach, the Institute leverages the resources of Penn State and the College of the Liberal Arts to conduct research on democracy and society, defend democratic practices, and foster democratic citizenship and educate for democratic engagement.Some of the regular activities of the Center include awarding the Brown Democracy Medal annually, publishing the Podcast “Democracy Works,” providing funding to support for faculty and student research, recruiting students in the Nevins Fellows program, and connecting with other institutions studying democracy. The institute supports two research centers, the Center for Democratic Deliberation and the Center for Research on Democratic Resilience.We seek a thoughtful Director who will lead the Center administratively and intellectually by supporting rigorous research on democracy, expanding the connections and research activities of the Center around campus, devising new research and outreach initiatives, engaging alumni to support the Center, growing the community of scholars engaged with the Center, and maintaining current signature activities. The Director manages four Institute staff (the managing director, communications specialist, podcast group manager, and administrative assistant).The Director will be expected to maintain an active research agenda and to be part of their academic unit and disciplinary community. A teaching release and supplement will be provided during the successful candidate's term as Director.Candidates for the Director of the Institute (Associate Professor rank) must have demonstrated excellence as a researcher, scholar, and teacher in a relevant field and have an established reputation in scholarly achievement.
